hero.headline: The future you’re longing for begins within.
hero.introduction: When painful experiences quietly organize life beneath the surface, moving forward can feel difficult even when you understand the pattern. There is another way to listen.
hero.locationLine: Online and in person on Kauaʻi
hero.imageAlt: Soft evening light over lush tropical foliage and the ocean on Kauaʻi

welcome.heading: What if you didn’t have to push past what hurts?
welcome.statement: Through Hakomi and mindful, body-centered therapy, I create a safe permission structure where difficult emotions can finally be felt, met, and transformed.
welcome.body: Here, nothing needs to be performed or perfected. We slow down and listen to the quiet intelligence of your present-moment experience, making room for what has felt too much to hold alone.

insight.heading: When insight alone hasn’t changed the pattern.
insight.lead: You may understand your patterns and still feel caught inside them.
insight.paragraphOne: You may have talked about your history, named the pattern, and worked hard to change it. Yet something inside may continue to respond as though the past is still present.
insight.paragraphTwo: Somatic work invites the body into the conversation. By gently noticing sensation, breath, posture, guesture, images and emotional textures, the beliefs organizing your experience may begin to reveal themselves.

approach.heading: Your body has been speaking all along.
approach.introduction: Hakomi is a mindful, body-centered approach. It helps us slow down enough to notice what words alone may not reach, following your own unfolding process with curiosity and compassion.

principles.title: Mindfulness
principles.description: Slowing down enough to notice what is happening, here and now.

principles.title: The body
principles.description: Listening for information held in sensation, breath, posture, and movement.

principles.title: Curiosity
principles.description: Meeting experience gently, without diagnosing, forcing, or rushing to fix it.

principles.title: Transformation
principles.description: We meet old beliefs and patterns where they live in the body and psyche and interacting with their particular medicine, message and meaning. Their symptoms can then be honored, integrated and transformed into wisdom.

permission.heading: A permission structure is something we create together.
permission.paragraphOne: Nothing is forced or rushed. Together, we create enough steadiness for experiences that have felt overwhelming, frightening, or inaccessible to emerge spontaneously.
permission.paragraphTwo: Your sense of safety is paramount. You remain an active participant. You can slow down, pause, or change direction at any moment.
permission.quote: I am an elder in age and experience and if there is anything I have learned, it's how to sit with my own, at times unyielding discomfort, and develop eyes that can see in the dark. It has created a certain capacity to sit with others who may be experiencing their own unyielding life challenges.

possibility.heading: When your inner architecture shifts, new possibilities become available.
items: Old patterns may begin to loosen.
Choice can appear where reaction once lived.
Hardened emotional patterns and moods may soften.

sessions.heading: Present. Collaborative. Gently paced.
sessions.introduction: Sessions last 60–90 minutes and take place online or in a private home office on Kauaʻi. No previous experience with mindfulness or somatic work is needed.
sessions.cardHeading: In a session, we may notice
items: Places of tension, openness, or movement

When trauma is involved, aborted fight or flight responses can get frozen in the body. We may work to simulate, physically or imaginally, a snapshot of when and how the survival impulse got thwarted and stuck in the nervous system. And then with infinite patience and honoring of the protective mechanisms of the psyche, we can follow some of those thwarted impulses into completion. Simultaneously we attend to the primal need for embodied safety. We may pendulate between these two poles until the trauma is resolved.
